To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel approach to learning representations that are useful for few-shot classification and sketch synthesis, and we demonstrate its effectiveness by exceeding state-of-the-art results on the Omnigilot and mini-ImageNets benchmarks.

we develop a novel sketching model that learns a visual representation of a large number of classes, that we show that this representation is extremely informative, and that we leverage it to produce high quality drawings of novel classes.

(a) we propose SketchEmbedNet, a model that learns a representation by producing sketches from pixels, (b) the embeddings learned by our model are informative for visual tasks, (c) we use our embeddings to achieve state-of-the-art unsupervised few shot classification on Omniglot and MiniImageNet, and (d) we use our model to generate high-quality sketches from a single image example
In summary, our research is concerned with
learning visual representations by imitating human sketches, and using these representations to solve visual tasks.
understanding and leveraging the visual understanding of sketching models.
the following question: \emph{can we learn a visual understanding of novel concepts by imitating drawings?}
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper proposes a novel approach for few-shot learning that is based on sketching and is able to outperform the current state-of-the-art.
our model is able to learn to produce novel concepts by imitating drawings, and that the embeddings it learns are highly informative for visual tasks.
our work is the first to learn a visual representation from a sketch domain that can be used in a wide variety of visual tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we learn a generative model of sketches and then show how the embeddings learned by the model can be used to perform few-shot classification.

we show that the embeddings learned in the sketch domain can be leveraged in other domains, and that the generative capacity learned in this domain can be leverged to produce sketches of novel classes.
our model can learn novel concepts by imitating drawings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a model trained to imitate drawings of objects across many classes can learn a useful visual representation that is transferable across domains and tasks.
the visual understanding learned from the sketch domain is highly transferable to the pixel domain and can be used to improve the performance of a number of visual tasks.
learning to sketch can be a useful tool to develop a general purpose visual understanding of the world.
